gh pr edit 520 -R punt-labs/ethos --body "## Summary

Privacy scrub of the repo's committed content — a one-time backfill; the write-path redaction feature keeps new records clean.

## Scope (explicit)

**In scope:** machine-specific home paths (all forms, including path slugs) and email addresses — in docs examples, test fixtures, and committed mission/session audit records.
**Out of scope, deliberately:** the operator's public product identity (name \`Jim Freeman\`, handle \`jfreeman\`, GitHub \`jmf-pobox\`). Ethos is an identity system and these are its committed content (\`.punt-labs/ethos/identities/jfreeman.yaml\` is tracked by design); scrubbing them from docs while shipping them as product data would be incoherent. Also retained: \`jdoe\` (a fictitious placeholder, not personal data).

## What happened during review (the interesting part)

1. The original hand-scrub (raw line-regex) had corrupted JSON in audit chunks; the audit-seal pre-commit hook refused them — fail-closed working as designed. Re-scrubbed escape-safely, every line machine-revalidated.
2. Reviewers correctly rejected keeping stale \`tool_input_hash\` values: the write path hashes the STORED redacted form, so hashes/previews are recomputed byte-faithfully (writer's own stdlib marshal, per-line verify) with \`redacted: true\` markers.
3. One corrupt chunk from the live session was quarantined via \`ethos audit quarantine\` (fully recovered; retired evidence itself scrubbed after review caught it re-leaking).
4. Review exposed a re-leak loop: each fix-commit's audit seal captured the fix commands, which contained the patterns being scrubbed. Closed by composing all scrub patterns at runtime from fragments plus a two-commit clean-window close, verified by a post-commit scan (zero remnants across all tracked chunks, including the chunk the final commit itself sealed).
5. Final round neutralized the personal email in redaction-test fixtures (29 occurrences, four files).

## Verification

- \`make check\` green before every commit (full suite, race detector, validate-content)
- Post-commit scans: zero path-form remnants, zero invalid JSON lines across all tracked session records
- The seal hook itself is the regression gate that caught the original corruption

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)" > /dev/null && echo body-updated

tool_input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import pathlib, subprocess
root = "<repo>"
addrs = ["[REDACTED:email]", "jmf@" + "pobox.com"]
neutral = "user@example.org"
hits = set()
for a in addrs:
    out = subprocess.run(["git","grep","-l",a], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=root)
    hits.update(f for f in out.stdout.split() if f)
keep = [f for f in sorted(hits) if not (f.startswith(".punt-labs/ethos/identities/") or f.startswith(".punt-labs/ethos/sessions/"))]
skipped = [f for f in sorted(hits) if f.startswith(".punt-labs/ethos/identities/")]
for f in keep:
    p = pathlib.Path(root)/f
    t = p.read_text()
    n = sum(t.count(a) for a in addrs)
    for a in addrs: t = t.replace(a, neutral)
    p.write_text(t)
    print("fixed", n, f)
print("retained (product identity):", skipped)
EOF
tool_input.description: Neutralize personal emails in all tracked files except identity records
